chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from 'Ali ibn Ya'qub, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

"I only instructed Aba al-Khattab to perform the Maghrib salat when the redness had disappeared, but he took it to mean the redness on the western side, and he used to pray when the twilight disappeared."

As for cases of excuses and impediments, it is permissible to delay it until a quarter of the night, according to the reports we have already presented about this, and what he narrated further clarifies that:

key_terms.الْأَعْذَارِ: valid excuses that affect normal legal timing
key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: the redness in the sky used as a sign for prayer timing
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the Maghrib salat, the sunset prayer
key_terms.الْمَوَانِعِ: obstacles or impediments preventing timely performance
key_terms.تَأْخِيرُهَا: delaying the prayer from its earlier time
key_terms.رُبُعِ اللَّيْلِ: a quarter of the night, the permitted delayed limit here

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Maghrib salat begin, and is it permissible to delay it due to an excuse?
ai.summary: This report discusses the proper timing of Maghrib salat and clarifies a misunderstanding regarding the disappearance of redness in the sky. It also states that in cases of valid excuses or obstacles, delaying the prayer until a quarter of the night is permissible.
